  - Colonial administrative records

**Also worth checking:**
- The **FamilySearch Research Wiki page for Kenya** — search "Kenya" on [familysearch.org/wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/wiki) — for a full breakdown of what survives, what's been digitized, and where originals are held (often the Kenya National Archives in Nairobi).

quirks: Schuylkill County was formed in 1811 from Berks and Northampton counties; pre-1811 records are filed under the parent counties.
Probate records (wills, administrations) are held by the county Register of Wills, available from 1811 - a primary parentage source naming heirs.

Roman Catholic parishes stayed under the Diocese of Philadelphia (an archdiocese from 1875) until the Diocese of Allentown was erected in 1961; the Diocese of Scranton, erected in 1868, took the northern counties, not Schuylkill. Sacramental registers are held at the parish/diocese, not the county.
Pennsylvania statewide civil birth/death registration did not begin until 1906; a 1908 death has a state certificate, but pre-1906 events rely on church, cemetery, and probate records.
Some naturalization and church films for the anthracite coal region are browse-only image groups (volume_search shows ~0% record-searchable) - browse image-by-image.

output.text_response:
Checking the current project state before routing this new evidence.

The project is researching whether Mary Ann Eastham (Jahue B. Burton's wife on FamilySearch) is the same woman as Polly Burton shown in the census records. There are 207 assertions extracted from eight sources, but none have yet been linked to tree persons — that is the next pending step for the main question.

You are reporting a record not yet in the project: an 1861 death record for a Robert Eastham in Pulaski County, Kentucky, naming his parents as James and Elizabeth Eastham, and noting that Robert was born about 1823 and appeared in two census records alongside the Burton household. That is exactly the kind of evidence that could anchor the Eastham family in Pulaski County and bear on who Mary Ann Eastham's people were.

Before I can extract it and weigh it against what the project already holds, I need the record's identifier. Do you have a FamilySearch ARK or record ID for that 1861 death record — the string that looks like `ark:/61903/1:1:XXXX-XXXX`? If you found it in a different collection or repository, a link or citation works too. Once I have that, I can pull it into the project and route the new evidence properly.

quirks: Pulaski County is listed in the FamilySearch burned counties table — an unknown portion of records was destroyed in a courthouse fire (date not stated in wiki); always check published marriage transcriptions (1787-1860, 1798-1910) before concluding a record never existed

Kentucky required county-level birth and death registration only in three windows: 1852-1862, 1874-1878, and 1892-1910; statewide registration did not begin until 1911. Events outside those windows produced no civil record; church and probate records are the primary alternatives
Kentucky took no state censuses — federal decennial censuses are the only enumeration series; the 1890 census is largely destroyed nationally

County-level marriage registration began in 1799; the FamilySearch County Marriages collection (1786-1965, collection 1804888, 3.38 million indexed records with images) is the first place to search for any Pulaski marriage
FamilySearch shows 102 total digitized volumes for Pulaski County; only the first page of that list was retrieved in this survey — additional volumes exist and were not examined
Neighboring counties to search for family members near county lines: Casey, Laurel, Lincoln, McCreary, Rockcastle, Russell, and Wayne
All records predating 12 December 1803 (county formation) are in Mason County, not Greenup County

Boyd County was carved from the northeastern portion of Greenup County on 16 February 1860 — events occurring in what is now Boyd County before that date are recorded in Greenup County; search Greenup first for any pre-1860 event for a Boyd County resident
The 1937 Ohio River flood caused a courthouse disaster that destroyed some pre-1937 Greenup County records; contact the County Clerk before concluding a specific record does not exist
Marriage bonds 1803-1862 are digitized at FamilySearch and 80-83% name-indexed with images — this is the strongest marriage record coverage for Greenup County
The Greenup County church records volume 1829-1908 at FamilySearch is browse-only: 0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable; must be examined image by image
Will books 1822-1895 at FamilySearch are full-text searchable but not name-indexed; search by surname keyword or browse images directly

Kentucky required county-level birth and death registration only 1852-1862, 1874-1878, and 1892-1910; a birth around 1823 in Greenup County would have no civil birth record at all; church records and probate are the primary alternatives

A person born in what is now Boyd County around 1823 would be recorded in Greenup County records, since Boyd County did not exist until 1860; search Greenup County marriage bonds (1803-1862) for any Eastham family connections
The 1951 History of Greenup County, Kentucky is available at the FamilySearch Digital Library and may name early Eastham family settlers

jurisdictions.name: Greenup, Kentucky, United States
jurisdictions.dateRange: before 1860 (primary parent for northeastern Boyd territory)

quirks: All events occurring in present-day Boyd County before 16 February 1860 are recorded in the parent counties — primarily Greenup County for the northeastern portion; search Greenup for any pre-1860 births, marriages, land, or court records
No courthouse disasters are known for Boyd County; original records from 1860 should be intact at the county clerk's office in Catlettsburg
A death in 1904 falls within the Kentucky county-level death registration window 1892-1910; check the county death register as well as the FamilySearch Deaths and Burials index (collection 1674848)
The Boyd County Library hosts a Kentucky Deaths Index database that may capture local deaths not in the statewide indexes — contact the library in Catlettsburg

The Ashland Daily Independent obituary index (Ancestry) covers 1922-1945, 1970-1973, and 1998-2010; a death in 1904 falls before the indexed range and requires microfilm at the Kentucky Historical Society
Fields Cemetery (the FamilySearch-claimed burial site) should be searched explicitly on FindAGrave and BillionGraves for a headstone or burial record
FamilySearch shows 41 total digitized volumes for Boyd County; only the first page of that list was retrieved in this survey — additional volumes exist and were not examined

Will books 1860-1962 and court minutes 1860-1869 are digitized at FamilySearch; a death around 1904 should generate an estate file if the deceased held property — check will books and administration files at the courthouse
